claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Increasing combustion pressure and modifying gas flow and gas mixture in the HVAF-i7 torch will increase particle velocity.
Real-time monitoring and shielding-gas adjustment can control particle temperature.
Spray distances of 300–350 mm are optimal for this HVAF-i7 FeCoNiCrAl process.
The modified process will remain effective for coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The resulting coating will remain effective under high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.
Faster particles transfer greater kinetic energy during impact.
Greater impact energy produces stronger splat flattening and improved inter-particle bonding.
Higher particle velocity increases particle momentum at impact.
Higher particle momentum promotes coating adhesion and layer buildup.
Greater particle kinetic energy increases deposition efficiency and coating thickness per pass.
Thermal monitoring and shielding adjustments will prevent excessive as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will produce a significantly thicker coating than standard-parameter HVAF-i7 deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock.
The intervention will produce a more adherent coating than the baseline process.
The modified coating will exhibit minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The modified coating will meet durability requirements for high-temperature thermal-barrier applications.
Baseline HVAF-i7 deposition produced coatings of acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
Exceeding optimized gas-flow or pressure limits may cause excessive oxidation or substrate damage.
The relationship between increased particle velocity and deposition efficiency is well supported.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thickness increase, or oxidation exceeding the control despite shielding adjustments, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.
